what: BXP owns premium office buildings in a handful of American cities: Boston, New York, San Francisco, Seattle and Washington. It owns the best buildings in each, not the average ones.
customers: Law firms, financial institutions, technology companies and government agencies leasing office space.
money: office rents in its five core markets
fees from joint ventures and third-party management
moat: Trophy buildings in locations where new construction is nearly impossible, which is where tenants have been moving as they leave older space.
risks: Office is the hardest property type in the world right now, with remote working still reducing demand
$10.2B of debt against $1.5B of cash, and refinancing office debt is expensive
San Francisco, one of its core markets, has been the weakest office market in America
opportunities: 8.4 times free cash flow with $1.3B of free cash flow against an $11.2B market value
Analysts see about 18% upside, with 20 covering the stock
Tenants leaving older buildings are consolidating into exactly the premium space BXP owns
watch: Leasing volumes and occupancy, particularly in San Francisco.
